reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates that magnetron sputtering of a Ti/Ni coating on diamond particles, followed by SPS, forms a diffusion-based interface that improves bonding and reduces defects in an HEA/diamond composite. However, the hypothesis extrapolates these findings to a completely different material system (W–Cu) and to thermal conductivity and irradiation performance, which are not addressed in the cited passages. The key premises about wetting, thermal resistance, and irradiation tolerance are unsupported by the provided evidence.
premises: Magnetron sputtering can deposit a Ti/Ni coating on a particulate phase
A Ti/Ni coating can promote interfacial diffusion and solid solution formation during SPS
Such an interfacial layer improves bonding strength and reduces interfacial defects
Improved interfacial bonding enhances composite density and mechanical properties
These mechanisms can be transferred from HEA/diamond to W–Cu composites
